claims.text: Standard stainless steel has reduced corrosion endurance under extreme corrosive conditions.
Laser Surface Alloying can incorporate corrosion-resistant elements such as molybdenum or chromium into the stainless-steel surface.
Laser Surface Alloying creates a homogenized surface-alloy layer on stainless steel.
Laser Surface Alloying produces a refined surface microstructure.
A laser power of approximately 2 kW, 10 ms pulses, and a scanning speed of 100 mm/s are suitable processing parameters for the proposed treatment.
Focused laser processing melts the stainless-steel surface and enables incorporation of corrosion-resistant elements.
Localized laser melting followed by rapid solidification induces in-situ surface alloying.
The alloyed surface has an enhanced concentration of corrosion-resistant elements.
The refined alloyed microstructure acts protectively and impedes corrosive attack.
The laser-alloyed surface layer slows corrosion propagation.
Laser Surface Alloying significantly improves stainless-steel corrosion resistance in extreme corrosive environments.
Laser-alloyed stainless steel will have a lower corrosion rate than untreated stainless steel under identical conditions.
Laser-alloyed stainless steel will have greater surface durability than untreated stainless steel under identical conditions.
The effectiveness of the laser-alloyed layer depends on the laser-processing parameters.
The effectiveness of the laser-alloyed layer may vary among different extreme corrosive environments.
Performance under conditions more severe than those tested remains unverified.
The long-term stability and consistency of the alloyed surface layer across varying extreme conditions are uncertain.
